knowledge:
- key_parameters: se=A SummarizedExperiment object containing 'coverage', 'dropoff_count', and 'dropoff_rate' assays ;; Nc=Integer specifying the number of control replicates ;; Nt=Integer specifying the number of treatment replicates ;; t=Numeric coverage threshold below which nucleotides are excluded ;; optimise=Optional tolerance parameter for EM optimization of Beta distribution shape parameters (default is NULL)
- alternatives: None mentioned
- when_to_use: When analyzing high-throughput RNA structure probing data with multiple replicates for both control and treatment conditions to statistically identify flexible/modified nucleotide positions.
- pitfalls: Drop-off rates of 0 are not allowed due to log transform, so positions with 0 drop-off counts in both replicates of a comparison are filtered out ;; Optimizing Beta distribution shape parameters using the EM algorithm (by setting the `optimise` parameter in `computeProbs`) is vulnerable to local minima; the current pipeline recommends leaving it as `NULL` (default) ;; For short molecules (like 18S rRNA), sequence bias correction should be omitted by passing a single stretch containing all positions to `nuclPosition` instead of pattern-specific positions.

workflows.name: bumhmm_structure_probing_analysis
workflows.intent: Compute per-nucleotide posterior probabilities of RNA modification from multi-replicate structure probing data.
input: se (SummarizedExperiment containing coverage, dropoff_count, and dropoff_rate assays for control and treatment replicates)
sequence (DNAString object representing the genomic/transcriptomic reference sequence)
workflows.stages: 1. Select nucleotide positions for pairwise comparisons using selectNuclPos ;; 2. Scale drop-off rates across replicates using scaleDOR ;; 3. Compute uninterrupted stretches of nucleotides using computeStretches ;; 4. Correct coverage bias (variance stabilization) using stabiliseVariance ;; 5. Define nucleotide positions for the null distribution (omitting sequence bias correction for short molecules) ;; 6. Compute posterior probabilities of modification using computeProbs ;; 7. Shift posterior probabilities up by one position to align with modification sites
workflows.code:
Nc <- Nt <- 3
t <- 1
nuclSelection <- selectNuclPos(se, Nc, Nt, t)
assay(se, "dropoff_rate") <- scaleDOR(se, nuclSelection, Nc, Nt)
stretches <- computeStretches(se, t)
varStab <- stabiliseVariance(se, nuclSelection, Nc, Nt)
LDR_C <- varStab$LDR_C
LDR_CT <- varStab$LDR_CT
nuclPosition <- list()
nuclPosition[[1]] <- 1:nchar(sequence)
posteriors <- computeProbs(LDR_C, LDR_CT, Nc, Nt, '+', nuclPosition,
                             nuclSelection$analysedC, nuclSelection$analysedCT,
                             stretches)
shifted_posteriors <- matrix(, nrow=dim(posteriors)[1], ncol=1)
shifted_posteriors[1:(length(shifted_posteriors) - 1)] <-
  posteriors[2:dim(posteriors)[1], 2]
